 1.

The present suit was instituted by the Plaintiffs against the Defendants viz. Lakhan Chowkidar (Defendant No.1), North Delhi Municipal Corporation, through its Commissioner (Defendant No. 2)
and TPDDL through its Chief Executive Engineer (Defendant No. 3), for the relief of recovery of damages amounting to Rs. 2,00,000 /-. However, on the very first date of hearing of the instant (2) Sh. Vijay Singh vs (1) Sh. Lakhan Chowkidar on 23 September, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97362530/
1 Suit, at the request of the plaintiffs themselves, the name of Defendant No. 3 (TPDDL) was directed to be deleted from the array of the parties and the suit was pursued only against Defendant No.1 and Defendant No. 2 by the plaintiffs.
2. Shorn of unnecessary details, the facts of the present Suit are that the Plaintiffs are the parents of a minor child namely Sunny, who was aged about four years at the time of the incident/accident, in respect of which damages have been claimed by way of filing of the instant suit.

sentences.text:
It has been averred in the plaint that on 29.06.2014, at about 07:00 PM to 07:30 PM, when the son of the Plaintiffs,
namely Master Sunny, went to play in a nearby park (Indira Park, Gali No. 8, Shalimar Village, New Delhi) along-with other children of the locality, he suffered grievous injuries, due to leakage of electric current from an Air Cooler, installed by the Defendants.

It has been stated that the Defendant No.1, was employed as a Chowkidar by the Defendant No. 2 /MCD, and that the Defendant No. 1 was residing in a pucca room, in the said public Park and one electricity meter was installed by the electric supply company (TPDDL), in order to supply electricity to the said pucca room.

It is claimed that the Defendant No. 1 had in an negligent manner, installed an Air Cooler,
outside the said pucca structure.

That the minor son of the plaintiffs while playing in the said park,
had come into contact with the stand of the said Air Cooler and due to the same, the son of the Plaintiffs, had received electric shock and resultantly, suffered severe burn injuries.

That upon getting the information regarding the incident/ CS No.60273/16 Pooja & Anr. Vs. Lakhan Chowkidar & Ors. 2/23 accident, the Plaintiff No. 1, who is the mother of the minor had rushed to the Indira Park and after she reached at the spot of the incident, Plaintiff No. 1 found his son was lying and was sticked with an iron patti, which was fixed under the said Cooler stand.

sentences.text: That the Plaintiff No. 1 somehow managed to separate his son from the said Cooler stand.

It is further claimed that at that time, the Defendant No. 1 namely Lakhan Chowkidar, was found to be sitting on a chair on the other side of the room, by the Plaintiff No. 1 and that the Defendant No. 1 had spoken to the Plaintiff No. 1 and had said, "why have you taken out the boy, let him die, then only you will come to know".

That subsequently, the matter was reported to local Police and one FIR bearing No.613/14, PS Shalimar Bagh, Delhi was also lodged against the Defendant No. 1, in respect of the offence punishable under section 337 IPC and the said FIR / matter was stated to be pending trial on the date of filing of the suit.

3. It has been specifically averred in the plaint that the son of the Plaintiffs, namely Master Sunny had got serious burn injuries due to electric shock due to leakage of electric current and which was a result of intentional carelessness on the part of the Defendant No. 1.

It has also been claimed by the plaintiffs that during the course of investigation of the FIR bearing No.613/14, the IO of the said FIR had found out that the Defendant No. 1 was employed as a Chowkidar in MCD Park and that he was on duty at the time of the incident and that the Defendant No. 1 had placed a private cooler and the same was being run/used by the Defendant No. 1, in an negligent manner.
That the son of the Plaintiffs was admitted to the hospital on 08.07.2014 and he remained under treatment for a period of one week.

That the son of the Plaintiffs, was still unwell and was taking continuous treatment from the hospital, in respect of the injuries, suffered by him, due to electric shock, even on the date of filing of the instant Suit.

It has been claimed that the Plaintiffs have spent a sum of more than Rs.50,000/-, CS No.60273/16 Pooja & Anr. Vs. Lakhan Chowkidar & Ors. 3/23 upon the treatment of their son namely master Sunny, for the injuries suffered by him in the incident in question.

That the accident/ incident in question took place due to the negligence of Defendant No.1 and that both the Defendants were jointly as well as severally liable to pay damages to the Plaintiffs, as claimed.

She deposed that her husband/ plaintiff No. 2 was a banana seller, who used to sell bananas on Rehdi.
She deposed that the incident in question took place on 29.06.2014, at about 08:30 PM, and at that time, she was present at her house.
She further deposed that her son namely Sunny had gone to Indira Park along-with other children including one girl namely Priya to play.
She deposed that the Defendant No.1 namely Lakhan was the care taker of the Park at the relevant time and he was also residing with his family in a room, which was constructed by MCD.
She deposed that she had received knowledge regarding the fact that her son had suffered electric shock from the Cooler from the child namely Priya.

She deposed that the Air Cooler, from which, her son had received electric shock was of Lakhan / Defendant No. 1 and the said Cooler CS No.60273/16 Pooja & Anr. Vs. Lakhan Chowkidar & Ors. 7/23 was affixed/ installed in the window of room of Lakhan/Defendant No. 1.
PW-1 deposed that at time of incident, there was boundary wall, all around the Park and that there was only one Gate to enter / exit the Park.
It was her version that when she reached at the spot, she saw that her son was lying in the stand of the Cooler and at that time, she had told Lakhan / Defendant No. 1 to switch off the Cooler.

At that time,
the Defendant No. 1 had replied by saying, "ise mar jane do tab tumhe pata chalega".
Upon hearing this, PW-1 had rolled her Saari from her hand and with the help of the same, PW-1 had removed her child from the stand of the Cooler.
PW-1 also deposed that when she was removing her son from the stand of the Cooler, she felt that there were some vibrations (Jhanjhanahat) in the body of her son.

She also deposed that the left side of the body of her son from under arms till the finger of the left foot had got burn injuries and resultantly, the little finger of the left foot of her son was removed.
PW-1 also deposed that the main door of the Park used to remain open till 09:00 PM and as per the sign board, installed within the premises of the Park, it was also mentioned that the Park used to remain open till 09:00 PM.

The maxim is stated in its classic form by Erle, C.J.: [Scott v. London & St.
Katherine Docks, (1865) 3 H&C 596, 601] "... where the thing is shown to be under the management of the defendant or his servants, and the accident is such as in the ordinary course of things does not happen if those who have the management use proper care, it affords reasonable evidence, in the ab- sence of explanation by the defendants, that the accident arose from want of care."
The maxim does not embody any rule of substantive law nor a rule of evidence.
It is perhaps not a rule of any kind but simply the caption to an ar- gument on the evidence.
Lord Shaw remarked that if the phrase had not been in Latin, nobody would have called it a principle [Ballard v. North British Rail- way Co., 1923 SC (HL) 43].

entities.text: Ballard v. North British Rail- way Co., 1923 SC (HL) 43]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The maxim is only a convenient label to apply to a set of circumstances in which the plaintiff proves a case so as to call for a re- buttal from the defendant,
without having to allege and prove any specific act or omission on the part of the defendant.

The principal function of the maxim is to prevent injustice which would result if a plaintiff were invariably com- pelled to prove the precise cause of the accident and the defendant responsible for it even when the facts bearing on these matters are at the outset unknown to him and often within the knowledge of the defendant.
But though the par- ties' relative access to evidence is an influential factor, it is not controlling.

Thus, the fact that the defendant is as much at a loss to explain the accident or himself died in it, does not preclude an adverse inference against him, if the odds otherwise point to his negligence (see John G. Fleming, The Law of Torts, CS No.60273/16 Pooja &
Anr. Vs. Lakhan Chowkidar & Ors. 19/23 4th Edn., p. 264).
The mere happening of the accident may be more consistent with the negligence on the part of the defendant than with other causes.

The maxim is based as common sense and its purpose is to do justice when the facts bearing on causation and on the care exercised by defendant are at the outset unknown to the plaintiff and are or ought to be within the knowledge of the defendant (see Barkway v. S. Wales Transo [(1950) 1 All ER 392, 399] ).

If the result, in the circumstances in which he proves it, makes it more probable than not that it was caused by the negligence of the defendants, the doctrine of res ipsa loquitur is said to apply, and the plaintiff will be entitled to succeed unless the defendant by evidence rebuts that prob- ability."

In any case, it is always open to the Defendant No. 2/ MCD to recover the amount awarded, if any, to the plaintiff from Defendant No. 1, in view of the fact that the incident-in-question took place due to negligence on part of the Defendant No. 1.
31.
Though, the plaintiffs have filed the instant suit claiming a sum of Rs 2 Lakhs, as damages/Compensation from the Defendants,
however, in their evidence, both the plaintiffs have testified that they have spent around Rs.
50,000/-, in respect of the treatment of their minor son, in respect of the injuries, received by him,
in the incident in question.
As discussed above, the right to recover damages that has accrued in favour of the plaintiffs, being the parents of the injured minor, is limited to the extent of recovering the costs/expenses incurred towards medical treatment of their son.

(II) Whether the present suit is barred by the provisions of Section 477/478 of the DMC Act?
The onus to prove this issue was upon the Defendant No.2 / MCD.

13 Defendants.
